name: Ṭūsī’s geometrical couple
description: Naṣīr al-Dīn al-Ṭūsī used a combination of circular motions to produce back-and-forth motion in a lunar model.

date.basis: Composition date inferred by historian F. Jamil Ragep from a colophon in a later manuscript; the manuscript is not the original.

events.statement: According to Ragep’s reading of a later manuscript colophon, Ṭūsī completed the Persian Ḥall with the rectilinear device in 1245.

evidence.supports: Ragep identifies the rectilinear device in the Ḥall and reads a manuscript colophon as dating its composition to late October 1245 in Tūn.

contributions.resource: Authored the Persian astronomical work containing the device.

evidence.supports: Ragep identifies the rectilinear device in the Ḥall and reads a manuscript colophon as dating its composition to late October 1245 in Tūn.

earliest_record.rationale: Historian’s reconstruction of composition from a later manuscript colophon; neither the copy date nor a global-priority claim.

caveats: This dates composition by a later manuscript witness, not the surviving copy itself. A related device was developed in later versions; dating and transmission to later European astronomy have been debated.

research.note: Independent review checked Ragep’s colophon interpretation, rectilinear model and composition date; other facets retain their prior status.
